claim.quote: We conclude that we have observed the top quark and measure its mass.

date.note: Public announcement date; the PRL paper (74, 2632) itself was arXiv-submitted 1995-03-02/03 (hep-ex/9503003) and formally published later in 1995 without a stated month on INSPIRE.
date.quote: On March 2, 1995, physicists at CDF and DZero announced the discovery of the top quark.

key_value_text.quote: We observed 17 events with an expected background of 3.8+/-0.6 events. The probability for an upward fluctuation of the background to produce the observed signal is 2.0E-6 (equivalent to 4.6 standard deviations).
key_value_text.value: 17 candidate events observed against an expected background of 3.8+/-0.6; probability of a background fluctuation 2.0e-6 (4.6 standard deviations)

name: Observation of the Top Quark
notes: result_type is "observation" (not "discovery"), matching the paper's own title "Observation of the Top Quark" (PRL 74, 2632), per instructions to follow the collaboration's own wording.

title/name capitalisation corrected in a 2026-09-17 verification pass (was "Observation of the top quark"); confirmed verbatim against journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.2632, whose title is "Observation of the Top Quark".

summary.plain: In 1995, the D0 experiment announced it had found clear evidence of the top quark, the heaviest and last of the six quarks predicted by the Standard Model, using collisions at Fermilab's Tevatron, at the same time as CDF.
summary.technical: D0 observation of the top quark in ppbar collisions at sqrt(s)=1.8 TeV with an integrated luminosity of about 50 pb^-1: 17 dilepton/single-lepton candidate events against an expected background of 3.8+/-0.6, a background-fluctuation probability of 2.0e-6 (4.6 standard deviations).

title: Observation of the top quark
why_it_matters: The top quark was the last of the six quarks of the Standard Model to be found; D0's independent observation, simultaneous with CDF's, cross-confirmed the discovery and let physicists begin measuring the top quark's properties.
